pins.time: 8:45pm, the match Mama Ronke struck has burned down to her fingers while Ronke laughs
9pm, the drizzle has eased but the air is still wet and close at about 27°C

9:15pm at Mama Ronke’s gate. Kazeem sets his cap on the cooler and asks Ronke whether she is the kind of woman a man would travel to the ends of the world for. She takes his wrist and turns his palm upward, smiling as if she has found the punchline but will make him work for it. The danfo engine catches before he can answer; he reaches for her before he reaches for his cap. Mama Ronke moves the lamp inside
9:30pm, the drizzle is still coming down at about 27°C
9:17pm. At Mama Ronke’s gate, the rainwater has gathered inside Kazeem’s cap. Ronke tips it out
7:40am, the same stop. The first danfo rush is gone and the second has not come. Kazeem has sold three sachets and given away five
9:05am, the lull after the second rush. Kazeem has gone quiet in the shade
5pm, and the rain has finally come down hard on the bus stop
6:50pm, the rain is easing to a drizzle and the street lights are buzzing on. Mama Ronke finally crossed the flooded road with her slippers in her hand

7:35pm and every streetlight on the street has died at once, so the only light is the kerosene lamp at Mama Ronke's gate and the glow of phones. Dinner is over. Kazeem washed his hands before he ate with them and still got scolded for talking with his mouth full about his trillion-naira plans. Now Mama Ronke has gone inside to find matches
8pm, still no light on the street
